problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following **cannot** be a root of the polynomial  $f(x)=2{x}^{3}+13{x}^{2}+10x-25?$
worked_solution:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients, the rational roots theorem states that any rational roots of the polynomial must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of the constant term}}{\text{factor of the leading coefficient}}.
$$

For the given polynomial $f(x),$ the constant term is $-25$ and the leading coefficient is $2.$ So, any rational roots of $f(x)$ must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of }-25}{\text{factor of }2}.
$$

Of the given answer choices, only $15$ does not take the above form. The value $15$ can be interpreted as a fraction $\frac{15}{1},$ and the numerator $(15)$ is not a factor of $-25.$
